correctness.rationale: The published fixed-grid formula reduces at \(d=2\) to a function of four occupancy counts. Under the null, cell labels are iid uniform and every length-\(N\) labeled path has probability \(4^{-N}\). The recurrence quotients only by label permutations and restores exact transition multiplicities. Its implementation agrees with brute force over all \(4^8\) short paths, uses exact rational arithmetic at \(N=128\), and exhaustively verifies the claimed support gap.

originality.rationale: The primary paper treats finite-horizon Ville-gap calibration numerically and estimates thresholds by simulation. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches found no exact finite-state calibration or the certified \(d=2,N=128\) boundary. The claim is narrower than the source paper and retains a stated historical-literature risk.
residual_risks: An older sequential multinomial, Pólya-urn, or Bayes-factor source may contain an equivalent state-compressed boundary recursion under terminology not recovered by the searches.
The numerical threshold is tied to the support-attained convention; over unrestricted real thresholds the rejection event is constant on the interval immediately above the preceding support value.

value.rationale: Finite-horizon recalibration is explicitly motivated by the primary paper as a power improvement when the sample budget is bounded, and \(N=128\) is one of its studied horizons. The recurrence removes Monte Carlo calibration error for a canonical fixed-grid martingale and compresses \(4^N\) paths to occupancy partitions, providing a reusable exact method rather than a routine numerical recomputation.
